newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends down again, technicals cloudy.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends down again, technicals cloudy.

text.p: London cocoa futures slipped back at the close on Thursday as the market lost its balance at the day's highs.
Traders, disappointed by last-minute bout of selling to knock prices down, said the losses could herald a move towards support at the lower end of a downtrend channel at 925 stg.

"People were disappointed that the market hasn't been able to bounce further," said one trader who explained the day's losses partly with fresh selling in anticipation that prices might drift off further.
Pressure also came from sterling which advanced slightly against the dollar from softer morning levels.
Traders said French-franc based producers such as the Ivory Coast or Cameroon could have been in the market but there was no firm evidence of origin selling.

At the close, the benchmark March contract had shed three stg to 937 stg a tonne after reaching the upper trendline at 943 stg early in light volume. The initial rally had sparked views that a move towards the technical 948 level was in the coming.
Volume totalled a moderate 5,662 lots, with switches being the dominant feature but the structure of the market was broadly unchanged.
Forward positions recorded losses of up to six stg.
Attentions remain on Ivorian cocoa shipments after the government approved a list of exporters for the new season. But traders say a safe crop scenario can only be drawn by the end of November.
Thursday's session saw a brisk 1,150 lots exchanging hands in the options market, mainly on December and May puts at a strike price of 950 stg.
Demand remained scant however in the physical market with buyers, put off by sterling's rally, hoping to tap cheaper prices.
